title: Volume Reduction on Idle Rates for High-Use EV Charging on a Parking License
content:
Training note. A Parking License that has drawn a large amount of charging energy recently carries a volume reduction on the hourly rate at which its billed idle hours are charged.

**What is the rule?** When the energy billed on the license in the 3 months before the handling date totals at least 300 kWh, the volume reduction is $2.00 per hour; when it totals at least 150 but less than 300 kWh, the volume reduction is $1.00 per hour; in every other case there is no volume reduction. The hourly idle rate is the standing idle rate less the volume reduction.

**Which energy counts?** The kWh on the EV charging energy lines posted on the license in the 3 months before the handling date — on-peak and off-peak lines of a dedicated charger and lines of the shared chargers alike — added together.

**Where do the steps fall?**

| Energy billed on the license in the 3 months before the handling date | Volume reduction |
|---|---|
| 300 kWh or more | $2.00 per hour |
| at least 150 kWh, less than 300 kWh | $1.00 per hour |
| less than 150 kWh | none |

At exactly 300 kWh the reduction is $2.00; at 299.9 kWh it is $1.00. At exactly 150 kWh it is $1.00; at 149.9 kWh there is none.

**What does it do to the rate? (hypothetical figures)** With a standing idle rate of $12.00 per hour and 320 kWh billed in the window, the hourly idle rate is $12.00 less $2.00, that is $10.00 per hour. With 180 kWh it is $11.00; with 90 kWh it stays $12.00.
